title: Component Spec
description: The build contract for one component (ADR-027): what it must be, read by the builder moments (/component-scaffold, /review-component). Selection and composition guidance stays in <Name>.usage.json, which /layout-generation reads. The spec owns states and accessibility; its token list is derived from styles. scripts/validate-spec.js checks every spec against the schema, its usage file, its props type and its CSS Module.

component.description: Component name; must match the folder and usage component.name.

anatomy.description: Every named part, top to bottom, including internal elements that are not ADR-023 parts. Names follow the ADR-023 naming contract (they are the Figma layer names). Every usage composition.parts entry must appear here.

parent.description: Anatomy name of the enclosing part. Omit for the outermost part.

element.description: Rendered HTML element, 'text' for a bare text node, or the library component it renders.

builtOn.description: Library component this part renders, when it renders one.

builtOnProps.description: Fixed props the part passes to its builtOn component (e.g. a Heading's size). Values the consumer controls belong in props instead.

role.description: Semantic role as exposed to assistive technology, or 'presentation' when hidden from it. An authored fact: design files cannot carry it.

action.description: What activating this part does. Interactive parts only.

when.description: Condition under which an optional part renders, in prop terms.

builtOnPart.description: For a part rendered inside its parent's builtOn component (not by this component): that component's own anatomy name for it, e.g. Icon. Located as [data-part=<parent>] [data-part=<builtOnPart>] (ADR-030).

notRendered.description: Why no anatomyExamples entry can render this part (it appears only after interaction, or has no element). The render test skips it; the docs overlay lists it as not shown.

anatomyExamples.description: Examples that together render every anatomy part (ADR-030), read by the render test, the docs anatomy overlay and the Figma parity plugin. One entry per example: root props, or a usage composition.patterns name for compound compositions (rendered from the same-named PascalCase export in <Name>.patterns.stories.tsx). Use several when parts exclude each other (a slot holding one of two parts).

props.description: Spec prop → value. Root props only; part props need a pattern.

pattern.description: A composition.patterns name in this component's usage.json.

props.description: The approved API proposal (ADR-026), kept. Keys are prop names; a part's props are keyed '<Part>.<prop>'. Every prop the component and its parts declare must appear; native attributes appear only when the contract depends on them.

options.description: variantAxis and lifecycle props: the allowed values. Must equal the TypeScript union and the usage variants axis.

default.description: Default value; null when the prop is off unless set.

concept.description: The ADR-026 vocabulary concept the prop belongs to, 'native' (a passed-through HTML attribute), or 'new term: <reason>'. spec:validate checks that the prop's name fits its concept (scripts/prop-vocabulary.js).

property.description: Figma property name. Differs from code only by casing or an ADR-026 recorded mapping.

set.description: Figma component set, when not the component's main set.

constraints.description: Prop combinations the component requires or forbids. Contextual misuse (where a component is placed) goes in <Name>.usage.json composition.donts. Content-format rules on a single prop are constraints too: lint when validate-layout checks literal values, else documented only (empty enforcedBy).

if.description: Prop → value that triggers the rule; '*' means any value is set.

ignore.description: Props that have no effect while the rule applies.

enforcedBy.description: What stops a violation: type (a TypeScript error), test (an a11y test asserts the behaviour or a @ts-expect-error case), lint (npm run lint or layout:validate). Empty means documented only: the validator reports it as a backlog item.

states.description: Every state, tagged with its ADR-025 kind. appData = the ADR-025 exception (interaction state held as a prop).

trigger.description: CSS pseudo-class for interaction states; the prop and value otherwise.

accessibility.description: The component's assistive-technology contract: role, ARIA attributes, keyboard. Moved here from metadata with the ADR-027 migration; a11y-coverage.js derives interactivity from it.

notes.description: Accessibility guidance specific to this component that the role/aria/keyboard fields don't capture.

styles.description: Anatomy part → ordered rules for that part's own element. Each rule sets CSS properties under a condition; later rules win. A value is a token path, a literal with a reason, a template embedding {token.paths}, or a reference to another property's value.

when.description: Prop → value, plus optional 'state' naming an entry in states. Empty object = always.

divergences.description: Known Figma ↔ code differences and the decision on each.

decisions.description: Per-component choices about how it is built, too small for an ADR. System-wide decisions stay in ADRs; cite one with adr when it applies. Read by the docs Spec page and /review-component, never by /component-scaffold (ADR-013).

adr.description: ADR id, e.g. ADR-023. Must resolve to a file in docs/decisions/.

ruledOut.description: Options considered and rejected for this component, so neither people nor agents propose them again without new evidence.

source.description: Where the option came from, e.g. a design system (Carbon, M3) or a review.

oneOf.description: Composite value with {token.path} references, e.g. drop-shadow(0 0 {size.halo} {color.icon.on-media.halo}).

sameAs.description: Another CSS property of the same part.
